IS:964-1956

METHODS FOR CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF SILVER SOLDER

0.

FOREWORD

0.1This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution

on 15 October 1956, on approval by the Engineering Division Council of the draft finalized on 11 September 1956 by the Basic Non-Ferrous Metals Sectional Committee.

0.2 The methods of analysis prescribed in this standard have been prepared with a view that they shall be useful as reference methods. Due consideration has been given in the preparation of this standard to the facilities available in the country for such analysis. 0.3 Taking into consideration the views of producers, consumers and testing authorities, the Sectional Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard felt that it should be related to the technological methods followed in the country in this field. This consideration led the Sectional Committee to, derive assistance from the 1950 Book of ASTM Methods for Chemical Analysis of Metals. 0.4 This standard is a necessary adjunct to Indian Standard Specification for Silver Solder ( *IS : 192-1956). Besides, this standard requires reference to the following Indian Standard Specifications: IS : 264- 1950 NITRIC ACID
tIS: 266-1950 SULPHURIC ACID
tIS

: 323-1952

RECTIFIED

SPIRIT

0.4.1 Wherever a reference to any specification mentioned under 0.4 appears in this standard, it shall be taken as a reference to the latest version of the specification. 0.5 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with tIS : 2-1949 Rules for Rounding Off Numerical Values.
*Suoerseded by IS

: 2927-1964 Specification for Brazing Alloys.

IS : 964 - 1956 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the methods of chemical analysis of various grades of-silver solder. The methods described deal with the determination of silver, copper, cadmium, and zinc.

4.2 ProcedureDissolve 1 g of the material, accurately weighed, into 20 ml of dilute nitric acid, and boil to expel brown fumes. If any precipitate of metastanic acid is formed, filter it off through a close texture paper and wash with hot water. ( It shall, however, be made sure before filtering that the precipitate was not due to contamination by chlorides from any source. ) Dilute the solution to 150 ml with water, heat and add dilute hydrochloric acid (3: 100) slowly and with constant stirring until precipitation is comTest the supernatant liquid plete. Allow to settle away from direct light. with 1 or 2 drops of dilute hydrochloric acid ( 3 : 100 ) to make sure that precipitation is complete. If no turbidity appears, filter through a weighed porcelain Gooch crucible or sintered glass crucible and wash the precipitate several times with dilute ' hvdrochloric acid ( 1 : 500). Dry the precipitate first at 90�C for 30 minutes and then at 180�C to constaut Cool in a desiccator and weigh as silver chloride ( Ag Cl). weight. 4.2.1 4.3 Reserve the filtrate for the determination of copper under 5.

6.2 Procedure-Heat the electrolyte reserved *under 5.3.1 to boiling, make slightly alkaline with dilute ammonium hydroxide solution and then just neutral with dilute sulphuric acid ( 1: 4). Add 25 ml of dilute sulphuric acid ( 1 : 4) in excess, dilute to 300 ml with water, bring to a boil, and pass hydrogen su!phide into the solution foi ,one hour allowing it to cool. If no precipitate appears within a few minutes, add dilute ammonium hydroxide solution drop by drop, until precipitation starts. Filter through a close texture paper and wash t#ce with warm water. Transfer as much of the Precipitate as possible to the beaker in which the precipitation was made and dissolve the precipitate in the beaker and on the paper in hot dilute hydrochloric acid. ..Wash the paper well with water. Add 10 ml of sulphuric acid (sp gr 1.84) to the solution and evaporate to white fumes. Cool, add 300 ml of, water and 5 g of ammonium chloride. Bring the solution to a boil and pass hydrogen sulphide for one hour. Filter, wash and dissolve the precipitate and repeat the sulphide precipitation as described above. Filter, wash and dissolve the final precipitate of cadmium sulphide in dilute hydrochloric acid as before and evaporate the solution to low bulk. Transfer to a weighted platinum crucible, add 10 ml of dilute sulphuric acid ( 1: 1) and evaporate to white fumes. If the solution darkens, cool, add a little water and 5 ml of nitric Remove the excess acid by heatacid and again evaporate to white fumes. ing carefully and increasing the heat to 500 to 600�C. Cool, dissolve the residue in a little water, evaporate carefully and heat again to 500 to 600�C. Cool in a desiccator and weigh as cadmium sulphate. *Since revised. 6
